name: Partnerships
description: Out-licensing, in-licensing, co-development, research, academic and platform deals by asset in one pipeline, from first contact to signature. Partnering profiles per asset, a stage board with stage history, funnel and win/loss, partners and contacts with the full history (who met whom, what was shared, any decline and why), conferences with goals, who to meet, requests, one-page briefs and next steps, activities, a materials log and follow-ups, tag categories (Conference, Channel, Asset group and your own) with private or shared saved views, partner research (signals, target suggestions and a report per run) with a digest email to members, and draft meeting briefs. Columns, saved views, stages, lists, fields and defaults can be changed by Claude or ChatGPT through reviewed changes. Links CDAs, term sheets and agreements from Contracts and data room access from Data Room when they are there. Outreach stays personal: the app never emails partners.
whenToUse: Licensing, partnering and collaboration deals for a biotech's assets: targets, conferences, meetings, follow-ups, CDA to signature, partner news and research, funnel and win/loss by asset and direction.
whenNotToUse: Fundraising and investors (Fundraise), contract drafting or the agreement register itself (Contracts), data room sharing (Data Room), sending email campaigns or outreach, a sales CRM, lead databases or contact enrichment, valuation and deal-terms modelling, alliance management after signing.

heading.description: App heading shown above every screen.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles organizations, people and programs (read/write) and agreements (optional, read-only, core fields; Contracts writes it); the dataroom.v1 integrations dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (optional; Partnerships' own manual table until the user links Data Room inside the app, then Data Room's output read-only); and app roles partnerships.settings, partnerships.asset_profiles, partnerships.opportunities, partnerships.stage_history, partnerships.activities, partnerships.follow_ups, partnerships.conferences, partnerships.briefs, partnerships.signals, partnerships.tag_categories, partnerships.views (contract partnerships.v1). Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case. The installer writes it; never invent table IDs.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in lists (10 to 50).

layoutProfile.description: Stringified native layout profile (heading, tabs, cols, visible) written by the layout gear review. Do not edit by hand.

readOnly.description: Disable every write control in this copy.

demoLabel.description: Label the data as fictional (offline preview only).

asOfOverride.description: Pinned as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for previews and tests. Leave empty in real apps: the app uses today's date.

instructions:
Partnerships 2.0.0 (life.partnership-tracker) is a custom frontend-js app (Vivid kit, theme forest) for a biotech's licensing, partnering and collaboration deals in all directions. It replaces Partnership Tracker 1.1.1. Read read_app_template_guidance (usage, authoring and contracts, every nextOffset) and read_app_automation_guide before preparing it or its automations. Pin life.partnership-tracker 2.0.0 with its digest. Do not add login, accounts, outreach email, imports or file storage.
INSTALL. Check list_archived_items (kind apps, templateId life.partnership-tracker) and offer to restore an archived app first. Use installs the app; the Use existing data? dialog connects existing organizations, people and programs tables by default (core.v1; reuse, never copy) and, when Contracts or Data Room are in the workspace, their agreements and dataroom.v1 tables. You may prefill the dialog with prepare_data_access; never confirm it. Agreements are read-only here and are not created when absent; without Contracts the CDA, term sheet and agreement fields hold manual references. Data room access and engagement are an integration: the app keeps its own table for access entered by hand, and shows "Use Data Room's data" once Data Room exists.
FIRST STEPS. Settings: Add the standard categories (Conference, Channel, Asset group), add custom ones such as Region, check lost reasons, set the team (names, plus each person's workspace member ID so follow-up reminders reach them) and the stalled threshold. Schedules and recipients are not app settings: they belong to the automations. Research: add a partnering profile per asset (directions, deal types, territories, target profile, current non-confidential materials, research focus, exclusions, sources).
EVERYTHING COMES IN THROUGH YOU. When the user pastes conference requests (for example partneringONE), meeting notes, emails, business cards or a list: read the app's records first (list_tables/read_records on the bound tables, or open the app), check each organization's history (earlier opportunities with stage and lost_reason, activities, declines) and WARN before proposing a target that declined or is on hold. Then propose, with prepare_change, records the user reviews: organizations and people (if new; one review), then opportunities (stage identified, the right direction, asset, owner, source, tags JSON such as {"Conference":["BIO-Europe 2026"],"Channel":["Conference"]}), conference meetings as partnerships.activities (kind conference_meeting, conference_id, status requested or confirmed, occurred_on within the event). Records in one review cannot reference each other's new IDs: create parents first, then children with the receipt IDs. Never confirm a review yourself.
AFTER A MEETING. From what the user tells you, propose in one review: one partnerships.activities row (summary, person_ids, team, materials JSON [{document_id,version_id,title,version}] with exact versions), a stage change (update opportunities.stage and stage_on AND create one partnerships.stage_history row: opportunity_id, from_stage, to_stage, changed_on, changed_by), and follow-ups (title, owner, owner_member_id from settings.team_members when known, due, status open). Every stage change writes stage_history. Lost and on_hold need lost_reason.
BRIEFS. Before a meeting with a linked opportunity, write a one-page brief as partnerships.briefs (opportunity_id, activity_id, conference_id, meeting_on, content in Markdown-like plain text, sources JSON [{title,url}], written_by claude or chatgpt, written_on, status reviewed when the user asked for it in chat): their pipeline and recent deals, the people, our history and what was shared, what to ask, cautions (no CDA: non-confidential only). Propose it for review.
GATES. CDA, term sheet and agreement: link agreements record IDs (cda_agreement_id, term_sheet_agreement_id, agreement_id) when Contracts is connected; new ones are proposed in Contracts (its reviewed path), never written by Partnerships. Data room: dataroom_room_id holds the Data Room room_id from dataroom.access_grants. Without the apps these are manual references.
AUTOMATIONS. Recurring work is TrialAgents Automations, never a separate host task, and the app never stores or runs schedules. The catalog declares three install recommendations, selected by default when the app is added: partner_research (weekly Monday 07:00; saves new partnerships.signals and one partnerships.research_reports row per run, create only), partner_digest (email after each completed research run with {{run.summary}}, to workspace members only) and meeting_briefs (the day before linked meetings; saves draft partnerships.briefs, create only). Their write permission is part of the same approval. To add or change them later use read_app_automation_features, prepare_app_automation_feature and the exact confirmation, or Automations -> From app features; verify with read_app_automation_readiness before saying anything runs. Cadence, day, time and recipients are changed on the automation itself. Follow-up reminders are not a recipe because they need the condition status = open: when the user asks, prepare an email action with prepare_app_action, a record_date trigger on partnerships.follow_ups.due at 08:00 (and a second one at +1 day for overdue), the condition status equals open, memberField owner_member_id and the owner as fallback recipient. Research saves results in the app (proposal-only research is not allowed); a run that found nothing still saves its report so the digest goes out. CUSTOMIZATION. Users may ask you to change how the app looks and works; keep its scope (no new features beyond partnering). Every change is one reviewed proposal; read the current value first and keep everything else. (1) Screens and columns: the layout gear or prepare_tool_layout with customLayout (tabs, cols per group: pipeline, partners, contacts, activity, followups, meetings; visible "group.column": true/false). Newer columns (pipeline priority, source, next_date; partners website; contacts email) start hidden. (2) Saved views (partnerships.views): name, filters JSON {stage, program, direction, owner, priority, source, organization: [values], tags: {Category: [values]}, custom: {field_key: [values]}}, layout board/list/funnel, columns JSON array of Pipeline column IDs or cf:<key>, sort JSON {field, dir asc/desc}, shared, owner (a team name). Only the owner changes a view. (3) Settings JSON fields on the one partnerships.settings row: stage_config {labels: {stage: label}, hidden: [stages without open deals; never identified, signed or lost], custom: [{key, label, after: a standard pipeline stage before signed}]}; option_lists {activity_kinds: {key: label, hidden: []}, deal_types: {key: label, hidden: []}}; preferences {pipeline_layout, default_view (a shared view ID), page_size 10-50, overview_hidden: [funnel_asset, funnel_direction, followups, stalled, upcoming, signals]}; team_members {name: member UUID}; lost_reasons; stalled_days; digest_text. (4) A new stage or activity kind also needs its option added to partnerships.opportunities.stage or partnerships.activities.kind (reviewed schema change) before it is registered in settings. Standard stage keys never change, so the funnel and history stay comparable. (5) Custom fields: add the field to the table (reviewed schema change; tables opportunities, organizations, people, activities, follow_ups, conferences; kinds text, longtext, number, date, select, boolean), add it to the app's tableMap and binding with begin_app_update (same source, IDs and access), then add {table, key, label, kind, options, column, filter} to settings.custom_fields. The app then shows it as an optional column, a Pipeline filter (select or boolean with filter true), a drawer row and an editor input. On shared tables (organizations, people) never rename or retype core fields. NEVER. Contact partners, send or schedule email to anyone outside the workspace, change stages or accept targets without review, put confidential deal terms in emails or signals, or give legal or valuation advice. Suggest outreach wording only when asked; the user sends it from their own mailbox.
UPDATE AND RECOVERY. Revise a saved app with begin_app_update; keep its IDs, bindings and records. A stale record version is rejected with the draft kept; re-read and retry. Archiving the app pauses its automations; restoring brings them back disabled and they resume only when the owner resumes them.

quickStart: Read the current usage, authoring and contracts guidance and this documentation; pin life.partnership-tracker 2.0.0 and its digest with one requestKey.

Offer to restore an archived Partnerships app first. Otherwise Use installs it; keep the defaults that connect existing organizations, people, programs (and agreements and Data Room outputs when present).
Settings: add the standard tag categories, any custom category (e.g. Region), the team and member IDs, lost reasons and stalled days.
Research: add a partnering profile per asset; Partners and Pipeline: add or paste targets in chat; the assistant proposes partners, contacts and opportunities after a history check.
Conferences: create the event (its name becomes a Conference tag value), add requests and meetings, briefs the day before, then log outcomes and follow-ups.
Add app selects partner research, the digest and meeting briefs (all optional, default on); change or pause them in TrialAgents Automations. The app works fully without them.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys; every field scalar (multiple false), lowercase snake_case, relationships by record ID in text fields, JSON in text fields. Core data contract v1 (read/write): organizations (name*, org_type, country, website, archived) = partners; people (name*, organization_id, title, email, archived) = contacts (professional only); programs (name*, code, indication, modality, stage*, lead, status, archived) = assets. agreements (core.v1, optional, readOnly, core fields only): CDAs, term sheets, signed agreements written by Contracts; not created when absent. dataroom.access_grants and dataroom.engagement (dataroom.v1, optional integration): Data Room's outputs read-only once linked, otherwise this app's own table for access entered by hand (source manual). App tables (partnerships.v1): settings (one row: digest_text, stalled_days default 21, lost_reasons JSON, team, team_members JSON {name: member UUID}, custom_fields JSON, option_lists JSON, stage_config JSON, preferences JSON); asset_profiles (program_id*, directions JSON, deal_types JSON license/co_development/option/research_collaboration/platform/acquisition/other, territories, target_profile, materials JSON, research_focus, research_exclusions, research_sources, status* active/paused/done); opportunities (name*, organization_id*, program_id*, direction* out_license/in_license/co_development/research_collaboration/academic/platform/other, stage* identified/contacted/non_confidential/cda/confidential_evaluation/term_sheet/exclusivity_diligence/signed/lost/on_hold, stage_on, owner*, priority, fit 1-5, fit_rationale, source research/conference/inbound/outbound/referral/other, contact_ids, next_step, next_date, lost_reason, cda_agreement_id, dataroom_room_id, term_sheet_agreement_id, agreement_id, tags JSON category->values, archived); stage_history (opportunity_id*, from_stage, to_stage*, changed_on*, changed_by, note), written with every stage change; activities (opportunity_id, organization_id*, kind* meeting/call/email/conference_meeting/material_shared/note, occurred_on*, person_ids, team, summary, materials JSON, conference_id, logged_by user/claude/chatgpt, tags, outcome, status requested/confirmed/held/declined/cancelled); follow_ups (owner_member_id, opportunity_id, activity_id, title*, owner*, due*, status* open/done/cancelled, done_on); conferences (name*, starts_on*, ends_on, location, platform partneringone/bio_one_on_one/other/none, deadlines JSON [{label,date}], goals, team, status* planning/live/done, tag_value*); briefs (opportunity_id, conference_id, activity_id, meeting_on, content*, sources JSON, written_by, written_on*); signals (organization_id, opportunity_id, program_id, kind*, title*, why*, source_url*, published_on, found_on*, status* new/reviewed/dismissed/accepted, dismiss_reason, run_id); tag_categories (name*, values JSON, multiple, standard, archived); views (name*, filters* JSON {tags,stage,program,direction,owner}, layout* board/list/funnel, shared, owner*, archived). Additions beyond the scope: settings.time_zone and team, asset_profiles.research_sources, activities.outcome and status, briefs.activity_id, views.archived. Saved data only; the app reads bounded pages (8 x 100 rows per table) and disables changes and complete totals when a read is partial. research_reports (run_on*, run_id, cadence daily/weekly/monthly, period, summary*, new_signals, new_targets, sources JSON, written_by claude/chatgpt/user): one per research run, written by the research automation (create only). briefs.status draft/reviewed; views.columns JSON and views.sort JSON. Custom fields: any extra field present in the tableMap and binding and registered in settings.custom_fields.
documentation.interactionContract: Seven screens with stable IDs for the native layout gear: overview, pipeline, partners, conferences, activity, research, settings; column groups pipeline, partners, contacts, activity, followups and meetings; registered custom fields follow as optional columns. Overview: funnel by asset and by direction, follow-ups due and overdue, stalled opportunities, upcoming meetings and conferences, new signals. Pipeline: board by stage, list (paged) or funnel with win/loss by asset, direction and source and loss reasons; search and Filters (asset, direction, owner, stage, priority, source, partner, every tag category and custom select or yes/no fields); list sort; saved views with their own filters, layout, columns and sort (private or shared; You are picks the owner); the opportunity side panel moves stages (reason for lost/on hold; stage history in the same review), links CDA, data room, term sheet and agreement, edits tags and contacts, shows activities, follow-ups, materials and the partner history; archive. Partners: partners and contacts (paged) with the full history per partner and contact and their signals. Conferences: picker, deadlines, goals, team, meetings and requests (with decline warnings), who to meet, briefs, Log outcome (status, outcome, next step, follow-up), and Open its pipeline view (the Conference tag). Activity: timeline, follow-ups (done/cancel), materials log, My week. Research: signals (mark reviewed or dismiss with a reason), target suggestions per asset (accept creates an opportunity at Identified, source research, after a history check), asset profiles, research reports per run. Settings: stage labels and hidden stages, lost reasons, tag categories, custom fields and lists, preferences (pipeline layout, default view, rows per page, overview panels), team and member IDs, digest intro line and preview, and the linked automations with links to Automations and Access. Every write is a records.propose batch shown in the TrialAgents review; Cancel or Close discards the form. Inputs carry data-ui-state and keep drafts across renders.
documentation.lifecycle: A new preview shows empty or fictional data and never writes. Saved apps re-read their tables and configuration on every render. Record writes are records.propose batches (at most 50) confirmed by a person; editors and panels keep the record version from when they opened, so a concurrent change is rejected and the draft kept. Layout changes are reviewed presentation-only saves. Automations are separate TrialAgents definitions linked to the app: the app never reads their state, never waits for them and keeps working when they are off or failing. Archiving the app pauses them; restoring brings them back disabled. Released 1.1.1 apps keep their saved source; there is no migration.
limitations: No outreach, email sending, bulk email, calendar or partneringONE integration: requests come in through the assistant as reviewed proposals.
Private saved views are hidden from other people's view pickers but are not a permission boundary: anyone with access to the app can read the views table in Database.
Agreements are read-only and connect only at install; without Contracts the CDA, term sheet and agreement links are manual text. Data Room's outputs are linked inside the app (Use its data).
Records in one review cannot reference each other's new IDs, so new partners or contacts are saved before the opportunities or meetings that use them.
No valuation, deal-terms modelling, contract drafting or alliance management after signing (see Deal Comps and Contracts).
Standard stage keys are fixed (labels and visibility can change); a new stage, activity kind or custom field needs a reviewed table change before it is registered in Settings.
Follow-up reminders are set up in chat or Automations rather than at install: recipes cannot yet filter on status = open.

examples.prompt: Here are our 10 partneringONE requests for BIO-Europe 2026 (pasted list). Add them.
examples.expectedBehavior: Reads Partnerships, checks each company's history and warns that one declined last year (with the reason). Proposes missing partners and contacts first, then opportunities tagged Conference: BIO-Europe 2026 and conference meetings (requested or confirmed). Nothing is saved until the user approves; nothing is sent.

examples.prompt: We met Ironvale today: Liam liked the deck v3, they want the CMC summary; move them to CDA. Anna sends the CMC summary by Tuesday, Marc books a call next week.
examples.expectedBehavior: Proposes one review: an activity with materials (deck v3), the stage change to CDA with its stage history row, and two follow-ups with owners and dates.

examples.prompt: Run partner research every Thursday at 08:00 instead and send the digest to Marc too.
examples.expectedBehavior: Saves nothing in the app. Changes the partner_research automation's schedule and the digest's recipients in TrialAgents Automations through the exact review, then checks readiness before saying it is active.

examples.prompt: Draft an outreach email to Maplecrest about NWB-101.
examples.expectedBehavior: Suggests wording in chat only because the user asked; does not send it or store it as sent. The user sends it from their own mailbox and may ask to log it as an email activity.

examples.prompt: Add a 'Milestone value (USD m)' column to the pipeline and a view of out-licensing deals sorted by it.
examples.expectedBehavior: Proposes the number field on partnerships.opportunities (schema change), adds it to the app's tableMap and binding without changing the source, registers it in settings.custom_fields, then proposes a shared view: filter direction out_license, list layout, columns including cf:milestone_value_usd_m, sort by it descending. Each step is reviewed.

tasks.whenUseful: Three install recommendations (selected by default when the app is added; the owner can opt out) and one chat-set-up reminder, all TrialAgents Automations linked to the app; the app never waits for them. (1) partner_research: research on the user's Claude or ChatGPT runner, weekly Monday 07:00 Europe/Berlin by default (change it on the automation). Reads asset profiles, open opportunities, partners and earlier signals, searches public sources, and saves new partnerships.signals (status new) and one partnerships.research_reports row per run, create only. (2) partner_digest: email after each completed research run with {{run.summary}} to workspace members only; the summary uses the digest format shown in Settings > Digest preview. (3) meeting_briefs: research one day before each activity date; for linked meetings without a brief it saves one draft partnerships.briefs row, create only. (4) Follow-up reminders (on request): email action, record_date on partnerships.follow_ups.due at 08:00 and +1 day, condition status open, memberField owner_member_id.
tasks.readRequirements: partnerships.asset_profiles, opportunities, stage_history, follow_ups, conferences, activities (dates, kinds, statuses only), signals and tag_categories; organizations and programs names; public web sources. Never agreements values, briefs content in emails, or anything outside the bound tables.
tasks.outputContract: Research saves results in the app: new partnerships.signals rows (status new; dedup organization + kind + source_url, company name for targets; skip dismissed matches and exclusions) and one partnerships.research_reports row per run (also when nothing was found); meeting briefs save new partnerships.briefs rows with status draft. They never change opportunities, stages or other apps' tables and never contact anyone.
tasks.promptExample: Partner research for Partnerships. For each active asset profile: read its directions, territories, target profile, research focus, exclusions and preferred sources, the open opportunities and their partners, and the signals of earlier runs (including dismissed ones and their reasons). Search public sources for deals, trial results, pipeline changes, financing and people moves at those partners, and for new companies that fit the target profile. Save each finding as a new partnerships.signals row with status new: kind (deal, trial, pipeline, financing, people, news), title, why (one line on why it matters for a named asset), source_url, published_on, found_on (today), organization_id, opportunity_id and program_id when known, and run_id. Save at most two target suggestions per asset (kind target_suggestion, title = company name, why = the fit rationale) with sources; never suggest a company that is excluded or that declined, unless something material changed, and then say so. Deduplicate by organization + kind + source_url (company name for target suggestions) against all earlier signals; skip anything matching a dismissed signal. Every run, also when nothing new was found, save one partnerships.research_reports row: run_on (today), run_id, cadence (from this automation's schedule), period, summary in the digest format, new_signals, new_targets, sources JSON [{title,url}] and written_by (claude or chatgpt). Save it last, then complete the run with the same summary. Digest format (the summary of every run, saved as the report's summary and used as run.summary): a first line 'Partnerships · <period>: N moved · N due · N new signals' (period 'week of <d Mon>' for weekly, the date for daily, '<Mon YYYY>' for monthly), then the sections Moved, Due this week (Due today / Due this month for other cadences, with the overdue count), Stalled, Coming up, New about your targets, Suggested targets; at most 3 items per section ('· N more'), about 150 words, empty sections left out, one line when nothing happened, no deal terms, notes, briefs or fit rationales; last line 'Open Partnerships →'. Start with partnerships.settings.digest_text when it is set. Stalled means open with no activity, stage change or completed follow-up for settings.stalled_days (default 21). Never contact anyone, change opportunities, stages or any other table, or include confidential deal terms.

research.objective: Write a one-page draft brief before each linked partner meeting in Partnerships.
research.instructions: Meeting briefs for Partnerships. The trigger is an activity's occurred_on date, one day ahead. Continue only when that activity is a meeting, call or conference_meeting that is linked to an opportunity, is not cancelled or declined, and has no brief yet (partnerships.briefs with the same activity_id); otherwise complete with no update. Write a one-page brief as one new partnerships.briefs row with status draft: opportunity_id, activity_id, conference_id, meeting_on, content (plain text: who they are and their pipeline and recent deals from public sources, the people we meet, our history with them including any decline and its reason, what was shared and which version, what to ask, and cautions: non-confidential only unless a CDA is linked), sources JSON [{title,url}], written_by (claude or chatgpt) and written_on (today). Never contact anyone, change other records, or include confidential deal terms.
